QF.id: AIFM CIII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_3

question.text: Satpura Market-Neutral Fund (close-ended, 5-year tenure) has 20 investors with total committed value of INR 300 crore. The Manager seeks approval to extend tenure by 2 years. Investors with INR 195 crore vote YES, INR 75 crore vote NO, INR 30 crore abstain. Is the 2/3rd-by-value approval under Regulation 13(4) obtained?

answer.text: No — abstentions are counted as NO, giving 195/300 = 65%

explanation.text: The Logic: Regulation 13(4) / the CTR Fund-Tenure-Extension row requires approval from at least two-thirds of unit holders BY VALUE of their investment — i.e., 66.67% of TOTAL invested value, not of votes cast. 195 / 300 = 65.00%, which falls short of 66.67%. The resolution fails. Abstentions function as non-consent. The Trap: Option A rounds two-thirds to 65% — wrong. Option C uses 'votes cast' denominator (mutual-fund style) — AIF Regulations use TOTAL value. Option D correctly fails but with a wrong reasoning (abstentions aren't 'counted as NO' — they just aren't counted as YES, which has the same arithmetic effect). Cross-Exam Context: XIX-D (Cat I/II Manager) tests the same 2/3-by-value tenure-extension rule — up to 2 years for a close-ended scheme. XIX-C tests both. Large-Value-Fund-for-Accredited-Investors can extend up to 5 years (Fourth Amendment 2024), still at the 2/3 by value threshold. Manager's Pro-Tip: Build the consent math on TOTAL invested value from day 1. Chase abstaining investors during the notice period — a silent investor at 5% of corpus can sink the extension vote. The Dissolution Period extension also uses the 2/3-by-value basis (then 75% by value for in-specie).
